claims.explanation: Triptolide kills cancer cells by covalently inhibiting XPB/ERCC3 in TFIIH, blocking RNA polymerase II transcription and triggering degradation of RNAP II; selectivity likely reflects dependence on high transcriptional output and intact apoptotic execution. Lines with high ERCC3/XPB expression, high MYC-driven transcriptional load, or intact caspase/apoptotic signaling should be most sensitive, whereas those with low ERCC3, high anti-apoptotic BCL2/MCL1, or defective caspase machinery should be protected.

features.basis: XPB/ERCC3 is the direct covalent target of triptolide; higher target expression increases drug engagement and Pol II inhibition
MYC-driven tumors have high transcriptional load and are more dependent on Pol II activity, so Pol II inhibition is more lethal
Anti-apoptotic BCL2 overexpression blunts apoptosis induced by transcriptional stress
MCL1 is a key anti-apoptotic resistance factor that prevents apoptosis after transcription inhibition
Loss-of-function caspase mutations impair apoptotic execution and cause chemoresistance
Caspase-3 mutations disable the execution phase of apoptosis, reducing triptolide killing
Caspase-9 mutations impair the intrinsic apoptotic pathway required for drug-induced death
IAP family members such as XIAP inhibit caspases and promote apoptosis resistance
Heat shock protein signaling is a resistance mechanism against apoptosis-inducing therapies
NF-kB activation supports survival; triptolide inhibits NF-kB, so high NF-kB activity may indicate dependence but also compensatory survival signaling
RELA/NF-kB is an annotated triptolide target; tumors with high RELA activity may be more dependent on the pathway triptolide inhibits
TP53 loss impairs apoptosis and is a common chemoresistance mechanism
